articles.title: Unpatched Tailscale SSH Flaws Could Let a Hacked Device Reach Root on Other Servers
articles.summary:
A single hacked device on a Tailscale network can be used to gain root access to other servers it can reach, according to a security researcher who published the findings this week.

The attack requires two things: Tailscale SSH set up to allow port forwarding, and an attacker who already controls one device that the network's access rules permit to connect to the target.

articles.title: Tailscale SSH Flaws Could Let Hackers Gain Root Access Across Servers From One Compromised Device
articles.summary:
A new security report warns that Tailscale SSH has flaws that could let a hacker move from one compromised device to root access on other servers. Tailscale SSH lets approved devices log in to each other over a private network. The report, called Tailworm, was published on October 25, 2026, by security researcher Erica Windisch […]

articles.title: Microsoft Teams to Use AI for Detecting Phishing Attacks Using Teams Conversations
articles.summary:
Microsoft is preparing to add AI phishing detection to Microsoft Teams, using conversation context to spot scams that may contain no harmful links or attachments. The feature will focus mainly on first conversations with external contacts, where attackers can pose as trusted support staff and ask employees to share sensitive information.
